chunks: Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad ibn al-Hakam, the brother of Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Umar ibn Yazeed, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, for Allah, on every night of the month of Ramadan, are those emancipated from the Fire, except the one who breaks his fast while consuming an intoxicant, or a bickerer, or the owner of the two kings. I said, 'And what is the 'owner of the two kings'?' He said, 'Chess.'

key_terms.صَاحِبَ شَاهَيْنِ: Owner of the two kings (referring to chess)

ai.seo_question: Who is excluded from the nightly emancipation from Hellfire during Ramadan according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) linking the spiritual liberation from Hellfire during Ramadan to specific behavioral and recreational sins. The term 'owner of the two kings' (Sahib al-Shahayn) is explicitly identified as chess players, highlighting the juristic concern with games of chance and distraction during the holy month. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on purifying both the body and the mind from worldly diversions to maximize spiritual reward.

en.hubeali:
Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muhammad Bin Al Hakam, a brother of Hisham Bin Al Hakam, from Umar Bin Yazeed, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said :

‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Emancipates (liberate) people during every night of the Month of Ramazan, Emancipating (liberating) them from the Fire, except the one who breaks Fast upon an intoxicant, or a bickerer, or an owner of the two kings’. I said, ‘And which thing is the ‘owner of the two kings’?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The chess’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ibn abu ‘Umayr has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Hakam brother of Hisham ibn al-Hakam from ‘Umar ibn Yazid who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

every night in the month of Ramadan Allah sets free from fire certain people, except those who break their fast with intoxicating substances, a heretic in religion and Sahib of Shahayn (player of the game with two kings). I then asked, ‘What is Sahib of Shahayn ?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is chess.’”
